title: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
summary: You get a list `nums` of positive integers and a positive integer `target`. Return the length of the shortest contiguous subarray whose sum is at least `target`. If no subarray reaches `target`, not even the whole list, return 0.

examples.explanation: [5, 9] sums to 14. No single number reaches 12, so nothing shorter works.
Even the whole list sums to only 7.

constraints: 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 10⁴, so every number is positive

approaches.twist: Grow the window until its sum reaches target, then shrink it from the left while it still does, keeping the shortest length.
Try every start, extend the subarray to the right until its sum reaches target, and keep the shortest length.
approaches.note: Works, but trying every start takes O(n²) time. The target is O(n).

approaches.twist: Build prefix sums, which only rise since every number is positive, and binary search each start for the first end that reaches target.
approaches.note: Works, because prefix sums of positive numbers only rise, but it takes O(n log n) time and O(n) space for the prefix sums. The target is O(n) time and O(1) space.

signals.meaning: Widening the window always raises its sum, and narrowing it always lowers it. That's what lets you move l forward once the goal is met, and never back.
The answer is one unbroken stretch, and you want the shortest one that meets the goal: shrink while the window still reaches target, and keep the smallest length.
Start the best length at float('inf'), above any real length, so the first window that qualifies replaces it. If it's still inf at the end, nothing qualified.

constraintReading: len(nums) can reach 10⁵, so trying every start and end, O(n²), means up to 5·10⁹ subarrays: too slow. Aim for O(n) time and O(1) space. The positive numbers make one pass enough: a window's sum only rises as it grows and only falls as it shrinks, so neither pointer ever moves back.

related.relation: Shrinks while its window breaks the rule and keeps the longest; here you shrink while the window still reaches target and keep the shortest.
